63.reasoning: From \(\frac{6}{7}\) to \(\frac{24}{7}\) there are 18 equal gaps, so each gap is \(\frac{1}{7}\). Counting gaps from \(\frac{6}{7}\): A is 1 gap on (\(\frac{7}{7}\)), B is 3 gaps on (\(\frac{9}{7}\)), E is 12 gaps on (\(\frac{18}{7}\)) and F is \(\frac{24}{7}\). So \(l(BE) = \frac{18}{7} - \frac{9}{7} = \frac{9}{7}\) and \(l(EF) = \frac{24}{7} - \frac{18}{7} = \frac{6}{7}\), and \(l(BE) - l(EF) = \frac{3}{7}\).
